source_text:
sic omnis gens peccatrix Aegyptus et Aethiopia a specie ad genus, quemadmodum etiam omne spectaculum concilium impiorum a genere ad speciemo
Ne quis argutari nos putet, ad principalem auctoritatem conuertar ipsius signaculi nostri. cum aquam ingressi Christianam fidem in legis suae uerba profitemur, renuntiasse nos diabolo et pompae et angelis eius ore nostro contestamur. quid erit summum atque praecipuum, in quo diabolus et pompae et angeli eius censeantur, quam idololatria ? ex qua, omnis immundus et nequam spiritus ut ita dixerim, quia nec diutius, de hoc. igitur si ex idololatria uniuersam spectaculorum para; turam constare constiterit, indubitate praeiudicatum erit etiam ad spectacula pertinere renuntiationis nostrae testimonium in lauacro, quae diabolo et pompae et angelis eius sint mancipata, scilicet per idololatrian. commemorabimus origines singulorum, quibus in cunabulis in saeculo adoleuerint, exinde titulos quorundam, quibus nominibus nuncupentur, exinde apparatus, quibus superstitionibus instruantur, tum loca, quibus praesidibus dicentur, tum artes, quibus auctoribus deputentur. si quid ex his non ad idolum pertinuerit, id neque ad idololatrian neque ad nostram eierationem pertinebit.
thought_title: From the general principle to the baptismal renunciation
orientation: Tertullian has just shown that Scripture's general condemnations include specific cases, and now turns to the authority of the baptismal renunciation itself.
pass_a_gloss: Thus every sinful nation is Egypt and Ethiopia from the species to the genus, just as also every show is a council of the impious from the genus to the species. Lest anyone think that we are quibbling, I will turn to the principal authority of our seal itself. When we have entered the water and profess the Christian faith in the words of its law, we testify with our own mouth that we have renounced the devil and his pomp and his angels. What will be the highest and foremost thing in which the devil and his pomp and his angels are reckoned, except idolatry? From which, every unclean and worthless spirit, so to speak, because not longer, about this. Therefore if it has been established that the whole apparatus of the shows consists of idolatry, it will have been judged beforehand without doubt that the testimony of our renunciation in the washing also pertains to the shows, which have been handed over to the devil and his pomp and his angels, namely through idolatry. We will call to mind the origins of each of them, in which cradles they grew up in the world, then the titles of certain ones, by which names they are called, then the apparatus, with which superstitions they are furnished, then the places, to which presiding deities they are dedicated, then the arts, to which authors they are assigned. If anything of these has not pertained to an idol, that will pertain neither to idolatry nor to our abjuration.

lemmas.gloss: they are reckoned, they are counted
it has been established, it is settled

choices.why: The glossary gives 'seal of faith' for signaculum fidei; here the possessive nostri ('our seal') refers to baptism as the seal of faith, so 'our seal' preserves the metaphor and the glossary term.
The glossary requires 'the devil's pomp' for pompa diaboli; here pompa stands alone but clearly refers to the same thing, so 'pomp' is used consistently.
The glossary mandates 'idolatry' for idololatria, and the term is central to the argument.
Lauacrum literally means 'washing' or 'bath' and refers to baptism; 'washing' preserves the literal sense while the context makes the reference clear.
Eieratio means a formal renunciation or abjuration under oath; 'abjuration' captures the solemn, binding character of the baptismal renunciation.
Apparatus here means the equipment, furnishings, or trappings of the shows; 'apparatus' is kept as a literal rendering that preserves the technical sense.

pass_b_english: Egypt and Ethiopia stand for every sinful nation, from the particular to the whole kind. In the same way, every show is a council of the impious, from the whole kind to the particular.

So that no one thinks I am splitting hairs, I will turn to the principal authority of our seal of faith itself. When we enter the water and profess the Christian faith in the words of its law, we testify with our own mouth that we have renounced the devil, the devil's pomp, and his angels. What will be the highest and most outstanding thing in which the devil, the devil's pomp, and his angels are reckoned, if not idolatry? Every unclean and wicked spirit, if I may put it that way, since I will not dwell on it longer, is reckoned in idolatry. Therefore, if it has been established that the entire apparatus of the shows consists of idolatry, it will without doubt have been judged beforehand that our renunciation in the washing also extends to the shows. For the shows have been handed over to the devil, the devil's pomp, and his angels, namely through idolatry. I will call to mind the origins of each of them, in what cradles they grew up in the world; then the titles of certain ones, by what names they are called; then their apparatus, with what superstitions they are furnished; then the places, to what presiding deities they are dedicated; then the arts, to what authors they are assigned. If any of these does not pertain to an idol, it will pertain neither to idolatry nor to our abjuration.
notes: The clause 'ex qua, omnis immundus et nequam spiritus ut ita dixerim, quia nec diutius, de hoc' is elliptical and possibly corrupt; the gloss renders it literally as far as possible without inventing missing text.

problems.quote: So that no one thinks I am splitting hairs
problems.why: Idiom 'splitting hairs' is anachronistic and jarring in context of patristic argument.
problems.fix: Use: 'So that no one thinks I am making fine distinctions'

fixed: Changed 'splitting hairs' to 'making fine distinctions' to avoid anachronistic idiom; source 'Ne quis argutari nos putet' means 'lest anyone think we are quibbling/making fine distinctions'.

problems.why: Inconsistent rendering of same Latin phrase; reader may miss they are identical.

problems.quote: So every sinful nation, Egypt and Ethiopia, moves from the particular to the general, just as every show is a council of the impious, moving from the general to the particular
problems.why: Sentence is elliptical and backward; 'moves from particular to general' is unexplained hermeneutical principle.
problems.fix: Explain: 'As Egypt and Ethiopia stand for every sinful nation, so every show is a council of the impious'.

problems.quote: renounced the devil and his pomp and his angels
problems.why: The baptismal renunciation formula shifts wording across sections, confusing a reader about the fixed liturgical phrase.
problems.fix: Use one consistent phrase for the baptismal renunciation throughout.
